newsitem.title: USA: Illinois GO bond bill fails in state House.
newsitem.headline: Illinois GO bond bill fails in state House.

text.p: Prospects for new general obligation bonding authorization for Illinois appeared dim Wednesday as a bonding bill failed in the state House.

The bill, which called for $610 million in new GO bonding authority mostly for prison projects, failed to attain a required three-fifths majority approval by two votes, according to a spokesman for House Speaker Lee Daniels, D-Elmhurst.
Republican members of the House introduced the bonding bill this week, the second week of the state's fall veto session.
The bill's introduction came in the wake of unsuccessful attempts by Republican Gov. Jim Edgar over the past two years to get a bonding bill passed due to opposition by Democratic lawmakers.

House Minority Leader Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, who is expected to become House speaker when a new legislature is sworn in in January, has said he would support GO bonding for prisons only. Madigan's bill, calling for $201 million of GO bonds for prison projects, is buried in the House Rules Committee, according to his spokesman.
